h1: Cast and Render — 3D & Games Landing Page Design
tagline: Landing page reference for a 3D, game or entertainment brand, captured at 1920x1432 with the layout, timings and palette specified in the brief.
summary: Landing page reference for a 3D, game or entertainment brand — looping video, scroll-triggered reveals and one self-contained HTML file.
about: Read Cast and Render as a landing page spec: the values were written down before the page was built. Colour is limited to neutral #F2F0EC underneath and near-black #0A0908 for the type, set in Inter. Delivery is one self-contained HTML file, captured at 1920x1432 so the frame is fixed before any code is written. Motion comes down to 3s transitions, cubic-bezier(.22.61.36,1) and a looping video bed. Treat it as the brief for a 3D, game or entertainment brand landing page that has to hold up under a rebuild, not just a first look.

layout.title: Navigation without a background
layout.body: A short run of links and a single action sit over the landing page, held at type from 12px to 15px and 560vh sections so the bar never competes with the composition behind it. Below 280px the links collapse instead of wrapping onto a second line.

layout.title: One media element carries the mood
layout.body: The clip runs 4.9s at 1920x1432 and loops without a visible cut, so it reads as surface rather than as footage. A poster frame at 1920x1432 holds the composition when autoplay is unavailable, so the layout never collapses.

layout.title: A list, not a card wall
layout.body: Features are set as a list in Inter rather than a grid of cards, which keeps the page dense and quick to scan on a narrow screen. The list is left-aligned to the same margin as the headline.

layout.title: Proof in one row
layout.body: A compact stats strip carries the claims that would otherwise need a paragraph, which keeps the landing page from turning into a feature list. The figures sit on the same baseline as the copy around them, so the row reads as one object. Cut a figure before you shrink the label.

motion.title: Sections arrive with scroll
motion.body: Scroll reveal is the only scroll behaviour in the brief, which keeps the page from feeling like a sequence of separate effects. Only one scroll behaviour is used, so the page never feels like a sequence of separate effects. Keep one scroll behaviour, not three.

motion.title: Timings in milliseconds
motion.body: The timings are short and consistent (3s using cubic-bezier(.22.61.36,1)), so hover and press states read as one system instead of a set of separate effects. Easing is specified alongside the duration (3s), so a rebuild cannot quietly substitute a different feel.

notes: The navigation collapses at max-width 280px and max-width 420px, so the bar has a designed narrow state.
Transitions are specified at 3s, which is the value to keep when the palette changes.
Font roles are assigned rather than mixed here, and 12–15px is the range the whole scale works in.

editorial.title: The numbers behind the landing page
editorial.body: 18,074 characters of brief produce a full specification. The load-bearing part is short: type from 12px to 15px, 560vh sections, 999px corners and 14px spacing steps. Nothing in this landing page depends on a default.

editorial.title: The order behind the landing page
editorial.body: Order is the design here. navigation, the announcement badge, the stats row, the feature list and the countdown are placed so the offer lands before the proof, and type from 12px to 15px and 560vh sections set the gap between them. A 3D reader gets the offer before the options.

editorial.title: What this landing page gets right
editorial.body: Compared with a template hero, the difference is what is missing. There is no card grid, no carousel and no second call to action: only navigation, the announcement badge, the stats row, the feature list and the countdown, sized against type from 12px to 15px and 560vh sections. Cast and Render states the offer once and lets the composition repeat it rather than adding a second claim.

faq.question: Can I rebuild the Cast and Render landing page in a different stack?
faq.answer: Cast and Render was built in one self-contained HTML file, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: How is this Cast and Render entry organised?
faq.answer: Everything quoted on the page comes from the captured 18,074-character brief rather than from a description written afterwards. That is why the numbers and the prose agree.

faq.question: What does the brief behind Cast and Render actually contain?
faq.answer: It is a build brief rather than a mood description: it names the composition at 1920x1432, the spacing and the motion values. Nothing in it treats the rendered image as the source of truth.

audience: Anyone using an AI builder who wants a brief that already contains cubic-bezier(.22.61.36,1) easing instead of leaving it to the model.
Made for studios that have to explain 280px behaviour to a client without building a prototype first.
